titles.title: Mesophotic reefs offer thermal refuge to the 2023 Caribbean mass bleaching event in the Cayman Islands

descriptions.description: Included are the raw data for vertical bleaching surveys that took place in Little Cayman Island, Cayman Islands, on September 16, 2023. Surveys were conducted on a shear vertical wall in the Bloody Bay Marine Park from 10m to 50m depth. All corals observed within 1m of either side of the transect tape were identified to species and assigned a health status (Bleached, Pale, or Healthy). Temperature along the vertical gradients was measured continuously with HoboProV temperature loggers. Code for data analysis included in submitted manuscript is also included.

Natural variation in colony orientation facilitates adaptive physiology of the coral Madracis pharensis in the Eastern Mediterranean

contributors.name: Bellworthy, Jessica
affiliation: Bar Ilan University Mina and Everard Goodman Faculty of Life Sciences

descriptions.description: The distribution of symbiotic scleractinian corals is driven, in part, by light availability, as host energy demands are partially met through translocation of photosynthate. Physiological plasticity in response to environmental conditions, such as light, enables expansion of distribution and resilience to changing conditions. Here we provide the data and the code used to compare the physiology, morphology, and molecular fingerprint of individual Madracis pharensis corals exposed to dramatically different light conditions based on colony orientation on the surface of a shipwreck at 30m depth in the Bay of Haifa, Israel. We found significant differences in symbiont species consortia, photophysiology, and stable isotopes, suggesting that these corals can adjust their metabolic physiology in response to light availability. These results highlight the potential of corals to switch to a predominantly heterotrophic diet when light availability and/or symbiont densities are too low to sustain sufficient photosynthesis, which may provide resilience for corals in the face of climate change.

Code associated with Schul et al. 2023 in PeerJ: Concordance of microbial and visual health indicators of white-band disease in nursery reared Caribbean coral Acropora cervicornis. Code is for dada2 processing of sequence data and use of phyloseq and vegan to analyze and visualize microbial community differences in healthy and diseased tissues of Acropora cervicornis with white band disease. We also compared healthy coral samples between 2017-2019. Raw sequence files are in the NCBI SRA database under bioprojects: PRJNA679809 and PRJNA308473
